title: ci(release): shard artifact catalog and emit deterministic provenance envelopes for private-installer
author: Diego Alvarez
description:
Motivation: Release indexes for the private-installer have grown to multiple MBs as we add more platform artifacts and per-arch builds. End-to-end signing of a monolithic index is slowing CI significantly and makes incremental uploads/retries brittle during releases. This change introduces a sharded release catalog and deterministic provenance envelopes per shard to enable parallel signing, faster retries, and atomic root-level verification in the installer.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces a sharded index format (index-v2) split by path prefix; the top-level 'release-manifest.json' references shard entries and a root envelope.
- Emits deterministic provenance envelopes for every shard (signed JSON-LD envelope that contains the artifact list, checksums, build metadata, and a canonicalization of the provenance payload).
- Adds a small root-signer step that signs the canonical digest of the concatenated shard envelopes producing an atomic release root signature. The installer verifies the root signature then verifies shard envelopes and artifacts.
- Parallelizes CI: new pipeline job release/shard-and-sign runs N parallel workers (per-shard) to build artifacts, compute checksums, produce envelopes, and cosign the envelopes using the release KMS key. A finalaggregation job uploads the root manifest.
- Terraform and upload integration: add a versioned storage layout and IAM role bindings to publish shards to the tenant GCS/S3 bucket. New tf module release_index_bucket exposes lifecycle rules and an ACL pattern used by the release pipeline.
- Installer/helm changes: private-installer helm chart now accepts indexRoot/manifestURL and performs layered verification (root signature -> shard envelopes -> artifact checksums).
- Rollback/upgrade tooling: add snapshot+delta support — each release manifest may include a 'prev_snapshot' pointer to enable partial rollbacks by reverting only affected shards.

Why deterministic envelopes: By canonicalizing provenance payloads and producing deterministic JSON-LD envelopes we make signatures reproducible across CI workers and avoid ordering-dependent verification failures in the installer.

Backward compatibility and migration: The new index-v2 is backward-compatible with installers that cannot verify shards: the release pipeline will also publish a compatibility 'flat-index' for a limited window (configurable TTL) while customers upgrade. No breaking API changes to hosted release endpoints.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalization, envelope generation, and signature verification added to release-ci.
- Integration test: staged release run against a test bucket and a private-installer dev cluster (helm chart installed with indexRoot pointing to the test manifest).
- Phased rollout: enable sharded manifests for internal cut releases for 2 weeks, then enable for external private-installer releases.

Security and key management: signing is done via KMS-wrapped ephemeral keys provisioned by the release controller; key rotation and audit annotations are emitted into the envelope metadata so we can trace which key signed which shard. Access to publish shards is limited to a dedicated release principal via new terraform module.

Files touched (high-level): release/cicd/pipeline.yml, release/cicd/shard_signer.py, release/tools/envelope.py, private-installer/helm/values.schema.yaml, private-installer/templates/verify-index.tpl, infra/terraform/modules/release_index_bucket, docs/release/shards.md, tests/release/test_shard_provenance.py

Notes: This PR focuses on the automation and format side of the change; artifact build optimizations (e.g., layer dedupe) are intentionally out of scope for now.
commits_summary: feat(release): add shard generator and envelope canonicalizer
feat(ci): parallel shard-and-sign job + aggregation step
chore(terraform): create release_index_bucket module and IAM bindings
feat(installer): verify root signature and shard envelopes in helm template
test(release): add unit/integration tests for provenance envelopes
review_conversation:
Sasha Patel: This looks promising. Two asks: show an example of the envelope JSON and make sure shard boundaries won't cause installer performance regressions.

Diego Alvarez: Added an example envelope in docs and added a streaming validation path in verify-index.tpl to iterate shards without loading all into memory. Also added perf notes and a small benchmark in tests.

Luca Romano: Terraform change looks good but please ensure the release principal has an explicit deny on deleting older shards (retention policy).

Diego Alvarez: Updated iam.tf to include a conditional lifecycle rule and explicit deny on objectDelete for 'protected/*' prefixes.

Priya Kapoor: CI flake on test_shard_provenance observed in the first run; reran the job and it passed. Approving now.

Merge: squash merging after green CI and a short hold window for infra review.
release_notes: Add sharded release index format (index-v2) and deterministic per-shard provenance envelopes; faster parallel signing and more robust incremental uploads for private-installer releases. Backwards compatibility: a flat-index is published for a configurable TTL to support older installers.
